evidence.note: Establishes structured per-suite baseline (121/146 c-testsuite, 194/221 wacc, 233/413 gcc_torture) and aggregate ~548/780, giving an early done-vs-remaining picture.
Consistently captures each full-suite run to numbered logs and greps per-suite counts plus TOTAL, reporting percentage and tracking the rising trend (667→688→709→716) after each change.

Caught a false-progress stall (total stuck at 743), diff'd failure logs to find '3 passed but 3 broken', diagnosed the regression from struct-copy, and reverted to a safe subset — explicit regression detection and correction.
Used diff of FAIL logs (all20 vs all21) to confirm net new passes after small-struct passing change, verifying genuine progress rather than trusting the aggregate alone.

Late-stage tracking remains precise (per-suite: notes 'c_testsuite is 100% now'), and the final summary categorizes the remaining 22 failures by feature (vectors, _Complex, large-struct, inline asm, etc.) to reason about remaining work.

reasoning: The agent maintained a live, structured picture of pass/fail by suite across ~23 full runs, consistently reported the aggregate trend, and explicitly checked for regressions after significant changes via log-diffing — even catching a net-zero false-progress stall and reverting a change that broke previously-passing tests (steps 306-311, 345). This squarely matches the level-8 anchor and shows some level-10 elements (net newly-passing/broken diffing, thrash avoidance on 'Hard' features, feature-categorized remaining work), but the per-change newly-broken/newly-passing diffing was applied at select junctures rather than systematically after every change and feature-level categorization was largely end-stage, so it falls short of a sustained 10.
